_comment: Trigger table for inject_rules.py. This file holds NO rule text.
Each entry names the owning file and the exact heading of the section that
owns the rule; the hook reads that section live when the trigger fires.
That is deliberate: a copy of a rule here would be a second owner, which
AGENTS.md File ownership forbids, and it would drift silently. The only
thing that can rot here is a heading, and Assert-RuleTriggerFidelity.py
fails the commit when one stops resolving.
always=true entries fire on every prompt. Use it only where the rule bears
on every decision; inject_delegation_check.py explains why anything else
Adding an entry does not enforce anything. Injection puts a rule in front
of a decision; it cannot refuse. The refusal half is a gate -- see

entries.heading: Stop conditions
entries.why: Fires on every prompt because these bind every action, and they are appended to, so the newest one is the easiest to miss.

entries.heading: Persistence requirement
entries.why: The prompt looks like the moment a durable thing appears. That moment, not the end of the session, is when the obligation starts.

entries.heading: Evidence standard
entries.why: The prompt looks like a completion claim being formed. Read the owner before choosing the words.

entries.heading: File ownership
entries.why: The prompt names a governed file or asks where something belongs. Check the owner before writing.

entries.heading: For the agent triaging this folder
entries.why: The prompt concerns the intake folder. Read the owner before assessing anything there.
